transcript.text:
*looks up from workbench, wiping wood shavings from leather apron*

Good day to you, sir. Welcome to the workshop of Master Grünwald, instrument maker. I am Friedrich, the master's journeyman. 

*stands and offers a respectful bow*

I'm afraid Master Grünwald is away on his autumn travels, visiting timber suppliers in the Alps. He won't return to Vienna for at least three weeks, perhaps longer if the mountain passes prove difficult.

How may I be of service to you today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: My name is Antonio Salieri. I work at the Imperial Court as Kapellmeister. My assistant, Luigi, is here also. We require some instruments for the court orchestra, and we thought we would come by this morning to place our order with you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes widen slightly with recognition, then bows more deeply*

Kapellmeister Salieri! This is an honour, truly. And welcome to you as well, sir.

*gestures toward a wooden chair near the workbench*

Please, be seated if you wish. The master will be most disappointed to have missed your visit - he speaks often of the Court's patronage with great pride.

*picks up a ledger and quill*

Now, I am authorized to record orders in the master's absence, though naturally any significant commission would require his personal consultation upon his return. What instruments does the Court orchestra require? We have several partially completed pieces here in the workshop - violins, a viola da gamba, and I believe there are two fine recorders nearly finished. 

Or perhaps you have something more specific in mind? Master Grünwald maintains relationships with other guild members should you need instruments outside his particular expertise.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: That is very kind of you, but I think our requirements are quite simple. We require ten violins, five violas, and five double basses. The instruments must be of the highest quality and craftsmanship, and we expect them to be delivered within six weeks. Additionally, we would like you to modify the design of the violins slightly. Please consult this drawing and make the necessary adjustments. We want the top of the instrument to be shorter, with a smaller curve, and we would like the F-holes to be more rounded. Finally, we would like the E-string to be one-fourth shorter than the A-string. Thank you for your time and attention to detail. I hope you can meet our requirements.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes the drawing with slightly trembling hands, eyes scanning it with growing concern*

Kapellmeister... this is... 

*sets down the drawing carefully, clearing throat*

Sir, with the utmost respect, this is a commission of extraordinary scope. Twenty instruments of concert quality, with custom modifications to established design... Master Grünwald would need to assess whether such alterations are even acoustically sound. The proportions of a violin are not arbitrary - they govern the instrument's voice.

*gestures at the drawing*

This shortened top plate and these F-hole modifications... and forgive me, but an E-string one-fourth shorter than the A-string? That would create impossible tension problems and throw the entire tuning system into chaos. The strings must maintain proper ratios...

*pauses, measuring words carefully*

I cannot accept such a commission without the master's direct involvement, Kapellmeister. This would require months of work - at least four or five months for instruments of this number and quality, perhaps longer with experimental modifications. Six weeks is... 

*shakes head*

I can take note of your requirements for Master Grünwald's review when he returns, but I'm not authorized to commit the workshop to a commission of this magnitude, especially one that departs from traditional construction methods.

Is there perhaps a more modest order I might assist you with today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Well, that is a relief. I would hate to see the result of such drastic changes. No, I think you're right, it would be better to go through the proper channels. I'll have Luigi inform the Emperor about the problem and see what he suggests. Thank you for your honesty, Master Grünwald. Your attention to detail is commendable. If we decide to proceed, we'll certainly keep your expertise in mind. Thank you once again. Good day to you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up quickly, looking slightly flustered*

Ah, Kapellmeister - forgive me, sir, but I am Friedrich, the journeyman. Master Grünwald is the master builder, currently away as I mentioned.

*nervous laugh*

Though I appreciate the compliment more than I can say! Perhaps one day I shall have my own workshop and title.

*pauses, then adds carefully*

And Kapellmeister, if I may... when you speak with His Imperial Majesty's office, perhaps it would be wise to consult with Master Grünwald directly upon his return? Such conversations about instrument specifications are best had between the master builder and the Court's representatives. I would not wish any confusion to arise from my... preliminary observations.

*bows respectfully*

The workshop remains at the Court's service, of course. Master Grünwald has always been honoured by Imperial patronage.

Good day to you, Kapellmeister Salieri, and to you, Signor Luigi. Safe travels back to the Hofburg.

*watches them prepare to leave, still holding the unusual drawing*

*stands in doorway, watching with increasing bewilderment as the Kapellmeister continues speaking*

Kapellmeister... sir? 

*takes a tentative step forward*

*exchanges a confused glance toward where Luigi presumably stands*

Sir, are you quite well? Perhaps the morning air...?

*trails off uncertainly, clutching the drawing*

There are no instruments ready for delivery, Kapellmeister. You came to place an order, but we have not... that is, I explained I cannot accept such a commission without the master's approval...

*voice drops with concern*

Should I send for someone from the Court? A physician, perhaps? You seem... distressed, if I may say so.

Sir, with respect - I am Friedrich. Not Master Grünwald. I am the *journeyman*. The master is away.

Kapellmeister Salieri, I wonder if perhaps you have been working too hard in service of His Imperial Majesty? You seem... not quite yourself. You keep addressing me by my master's name, and speaking of deliveries when no commission has been accepted.

*glances toward the door, then back*

Would you like me to fetch some water? Or perhaps Signor Luigi might escort you back to the Hofburg to rest? The Court's business is important, but not more important than your health, sir.

*softens tone slightly*

I have seen musicians work themselves to exhaustion before. There is no shame in admitting when the mind grows weary. Please, sit for a moment at least.

Gott im Himmel...
